_notes: Sheet 176 of the tournament savegame (8x4), read card by card from the image on 2026-11-22. CardID = 17600 + idx; 308 = character card (sheet 3, 10x7, index 8). The deck object of the save holds 31 cards: the 30 of the deck plus the character card, hence card_count 31 and card_ids [308, 17629] in the catalog. Sheet 176 is also Medusa's, the turtles' and the other heroes': only deck.identity (data/tts/robin-hood.json) tells the decks apart (docs/card-identity.md).

Hero card (read from the image): ROBIN HOOD, RANGED, START HEALTH 13, MOVE 2, special ability "After you attack, you may move your attacking fighter up to 2 spaces."; sidekick OUTLAWS, MELEE, START HEALTH 1 x4. The bag holds four Custom_Token objects nicknamed Outlaw (one image, no second face, no life dial), the miniature (Custom_Model 5aa21a) and the life dial (Custom_Model 1fc8df, description Hero Health, MAX_VALUE 13).

Bands read from the images: ROBIN HOOD on A Hunter's Eye, Piercing Shot, Disarming Shot and Steal From the Rich; OUTLAW on Highway Robbery (only an Outlaw plays it); ANY on Ambush, Regroup, Feint, Snark, Wily Fighting and Defenders of Sherwood. Order on the sheet: A Hunter's Eye 0-2, Piercing Shot 3-4, Disarming Shot 5-6, Ambush 7-8, Highway Robbery 9-12, Regroup 13-15, Feint 16-18, Snark 19-21, Wily Fighting 22-24, Defenders of Sherwood 25-26, Steal From the Rich 27-29.

Titles, types, printed values, BOOSTs, copies and texts of the 11 titles agree with unmatched-memory (30 cards); unmatched-memory has no restriction band, the overlay carries it. The save's life dial 1fc8df is also Yennenga's dial (a Custom_Model named after its hero) and a miniature of Nikola Tesla (not in the project): told apart by name (docs/card-identity.md, Piece identity).

Robin Hood's Feint (idx 16-18, ANY, 2 / BOOST 2) is word for word Bigfoot's Feint (and Pandora's, which carries a tag), so its three cards carry the tag robin-hood: two equal Card values in two decks of one sheet are forbidden by tests/test_card_identity.py. Nothing reads the tag.
Ambush: the card prints "this card's value" (unmatched-memory: "this card's attack value"), so the overlay carries the printed text.
